description:
Observed 2026-08-14 on the Arch host (teddy0@snrsiDesktop).

SYMPTOM. 'cargo test --release -p outram-park-digital-twin-engine --lib --tests --examples' failed once with:
  test a_remote_client_can_drive_the_ciet_loop ... FAILED
  test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed  finished in 2.01s

The 2.01 s is the tell: the passing runs take 16.5-19.1 s, so it did not run the loop and fail an assertion -- it fell over almost immediately, consistent with a failure to bind or connect rather than a physics or control problem.

NOT REPRODUCIBLE ON DEMAND. Immediately afterwards:
  - alone ('--test ciet_v2_headless_remote_control'): PASSED, 17.08 s
  - full suite again, unchanged tree: PASSED, 18.58 s
Every other run in the same session passed (16.56 s, 19.08 s, 18.58 s). So it is intermittent and only seen under the full parallel suite. Maintainer's read, same day: 'it's likely a race condition' -- agreed.

WHY A RACE IS PLAUSIBLE. Two OPC-UA integration tests run as separate binaries and cargo runs them concurrently: ciet_v2_headless_remote_control and ciet_v2_opcua_roundtrip. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/opcua_core/server.rs already isolates the certificate store PER PORT (instance_pki_dir(profile.pki_dir_name, format!('port-{}', config.port))) with the comment that this makes concurrent instances -- 'notably headless simulator tests' -- stop racing on one shared keypair. That mitigation assumes the two tests pick DIFFERENT ports. Worth checking:
  1. Do the two tests actually use different ports, or does one pick a fixed port that can collide with a previous run's server still shutting down? Note OpcuaServerHandle::shutdown() signals and returns immediately -- the thread and its listening socket close 'shortly afterwards', so a fast re-bind can land before the old socket is released (no SO_REUSEADDR is evident).
  2. Is there mDNS discovery contention (MdnsAdvertisement is withdrawn on DROP, not on shutdown())?
  3. Does the client retry, or connect once and give up?

WHAT NOT TO DO. Do not 'fix' it by serialising the suite or adding a sleep -- that hides the race and slows an already-slow suite. If the ports can collide, bind an ephemeral port per test and read it back from OpcuaEndpointInfo.

CAPTURE THE FAILURE OUTPUT NEXT TIME IT HAPPENS -- this report has the timing and the exit, but not the error text, because the run was grepped for 'test result' lines. Re-run with the full output retained.
title: ciet_v2_headless_remote_control: intermittent failure under the full parallel suite -- likely an OPC-UA port/PKI race

design:
Child epic of the nuclear refinery programme (bn op-upme).

**Fidelity target: Engineering model (infrastructure)**

**Audit before building. Most of this exists.**

Already present in `src/reactions.rs`: `langmuir_hinshelwood_rate`,
`with_langmuir_hinshelwood`, `adsorption_constant`, `denominator_value`,
`forward_rate_constant`, `reverse_rate_constant`, `equilibrium_constant`,
`with_reaction_heat`, `with_conversion`, `ReactionKind`, `ReactionBasis`,
`EquilibriumConstant`.

Already present in `src/reactors/`: `Pfr`, `Cstr`, `ConversionReactor`,
`EquilibriumReactor`, `GibbsReactor`, `ReactorFeed`, `ReactorOutcome`.

**The programme asked for "a reusable LHHW catalytic kinetic framework rather
than refinery-unit-specific equations". It exists.**

## What is actually missing

Not the machinery -- the **reaction networks and chemistry data** that use it,
and the ergonomics of composing them. Likely real work:

- `ReactionSet` / network composition and its public API
- heterogeneous catalytic reaction ergonomics on top of existing LHHW
- packed-bed application of the existing `Pfr`
- reaction-enthalpy bookkeeping into the global energy ledger
- **elemental conservation checks on every reacting unit**

Gates hydrotreating, hydrocracking and FCC.

## Out of scope for this pass (programme-wide)

Do not: port DWSIM UI or graphical flowsheet objects; port CAPE-OPEN unless a
concrete backend requirement exists; reproduce .NET class architecture; make
DWSIM depend on Outram-FOAM; solve thousands of molecular species in the CDU;
implement molecular reconstruction before assay/pseudocomponent CDU works; call
a converged model validated without reference evidence; hide conservation
errors; push to `main`.
title: Refinery: Reaction and chemical-thermo infrastructure

description:
Stale claim found 2026-08-11. docs/notes.md still describes quality_bubble_point_subcooled as "the active failing test", but cargo test --release -p tampines-steam-tables --lib --tests reports 924 passed, 0 failed, 14 ignored.

Either the test was fixed and the note never updated, or it is one of the 14 ignored and the note should say so. Determine which and correct it.

Small, but it is the same class as the Marviken claims and the op-r6ns scaffold-only drift: documentation asserting a state the code no longer has. A reader trusting that note would waste time hunting a failure that does not exist, or worse, assume other claims in the same file are equally stale.

Also worth noting from the same session: the Edwards-O Brien blowdown integration test takes 897 seconds -- nearly 15 minutes -- which is why full-suite runs kept hitting timeouts. That is expected for what it does, but it belongs in the crate testing notes so nobody reports a timeout as a failure. Compare the workspace CLAUDE.md rule added today for the TUAS natural-circulation suite.
title: tampines-steam-tables: docs/notes.md calls a passing test the active failing test

design:
Part of the dwsim-libs maturity epic (bn op-otqe).

Apply the mature-crate rule:

> **If it is too complex for Haiku to use correctly through the public API, it
> is a bad API.**

## Checklist

- [ ] `prelude::*` exposes the **complete critical workflow** — the crate
      currently has **no prelude at all**, so this starts from zero
- [ ] `BlackOilCrude` is discoverable
- [ ] pseudo-component characterization is discoverable
- [ ] flash / property-package selection is discoverable
- [ ] crude-column construction is discoverable
- [ ] `solve_crude_column` is discoverable
- [ ] result objects expose useful engineering quantities **directly**
- [ ] units are explicit in names and rustdoc
- [ ] errors explain **invalid configurations**, not just failure
- [ ] material and component balances are easy to inspect
- [ ] energy duties are easy to inspect
- [ ] **downstream unit operations can consume upstream product streams without
      manual reconstruction**

## Two design constraints

**Avoid giant generic dictionaries or untyped arrays where domain-specific
result objects already make sense.** A `HashMap<String, f64>` of results is
undiscoverable by construction: nothing completes, nothing type-checks, and
every key is a guess. This is the same class of defect as a prelude that
exports module paths instead of symbols (#58) — the information exists but
cannot be found.

**The last checklist item is load-bearing and outlives this crate.** HTGR heat
will later replace or supplement refinery fired-heater duties, so enthalpy and
stream identity must survive unit-operation boundaries. If
`cdu.atmospheric_residue()` returns a flow rate rather than a stream, the VDU
cannot consume it, and the design has to be undone the moment a second unit is
chained.

## Evidence base

Every line above earned its place in #58 across seven crates. The pattern
without exception: **the type was exported, but the way in was not shown.** The
two worst were a prelude that imported nothing (empty scope, no error) and a
prelude that exported a `todo!()` which panics.

Add a **regression test per discovered defect**. Doc tests are preferred where
the defect concerns discoverability, since they make the intended usage
executable rather than asserted, and they fail if the seam is removed again.
title: dwsim-libs: public API quality gate and stream-consumability
